newsitem.title: UK: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 24.
newsitem.headline: Worldwide Advertising & Media Digest - June 24.

text.p: ....REUTERS WORLDWIDE ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST.....
Reuters news from around the world on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends ***********************************************
ADVERTISING & MARKETING:

LONDON - Bans on tobacco advertising will force cigarette makers to seek marketing opportunities by exploiting loopholes, say industry experts. Tobacco companies are already promoting their brands in British bars and clubs where free samples are distributed to smokers. In New York, lawyers poring over restrictions that will ban tobacco advertising in the U.S. say it could be years before the first Joe Camel billboard comes down.

CANNES - U.S.-based advertising agency Foote Cone & Belding says it's in a stronger position to win global accounts since its parent company, True North Communications, recently ended its alliance with Paris-based Publicis. "Dissolving the alliance gave us back ownership of the network," says Geoff Thompson, worldwide creative director for FCB.

NEW YORK - A settlement with the U.S. Federal Trade Commission may require Exxon Corp to begin running ads that refute its own claims that its petrol lowers the cost of car maintenance, the Wall Street Journal reports.

CANNES - The two giants of French advertising, Havas Advertising and Publicis, give contrasting outlooks for advertising in France following the recent French parliamentary elections. Havas Advertising's turnover is growing faster than earlier forecast, says Havas Advertising Vice Chairman Jean-Michel Carlo.

BERLIN - German commercial TV channel Sat.1 rejects a magazine report claiming that it faces millions of marks in fines for showing too many commercials during its airtime. The company says allegations of excessive advertising were made years ago and that media authorities have not decided on the issue. The statement follows a report in the news magazine Focus that Sat.1 faced 15.8 million marks ($9.2 million) in fines.

NEW YORK - The American Society of Magazine Editors expresses concern over what it describes as a "trend among some magazines to give advertisers advance notice of upcoming articles". ASME President Frank Lalli, says several publishers "routinely alert advertisers about upcoming articles so that advertisers can decide whether to reschedule, or even pull, their ads".
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BRUSSELS - A new European Union broadcasting law has been passed. The "Television Without Frontiers" directive for the first time guarantees viewers in the European Union the right to watch major sporting events free, even if exclusive rights have been bought by pay television channels.

MUNICH - The Kirch Group is holding talks with France's Canal-Plus about the German and the Italian pay-TV markets, according to a Kirch spokesman. Kirch and Bertelsmann affiliate CLT-UFA announced they planned to operate German pay-TV broadcaster Premiere as a 50-50 venture. A joint statement said Canal-Plus, which holds 37.5 percent of Premiere, was satisfied with the deal. Canal-Plus declined to comment.
NEW DELHI - India's broadcast regulator, which will be set up under a planned law to free up the air waves, will have the power to enforce competition, says India's Broadcasting minister.

MUNICH - ProSieben Media AG offers investors a relatively cheap entry into Germany's media sector by saying new shares in the commercial TV channel will cost no more than 72 marks. Following weeks of a high-profile media campaign modelled after a successful marketing blitz by phone giant Deutsche Telekom, ProSieben says the price for its shares will be set through a bookbuilding phase at between 66-72 marks. The final offer price for the 17.5 million non-voting preference shares will be set over the next two weeks. Share trade begins on July 7.
BRUSSELS - The European Commission is expected to tell Belgium this week that it must scrap an advertising monopoly granted to Flemish TV channel VTM or else face legal action.

LONDON - England's top soccer clubs have been advised to set up their own TV service when a deal with satellite broadcaster BSkyB expires in 2001, the Financial Times reported. The share price of BSkyB dropped on the London Stock Exchange after the FT published the article, which described a consultants' report to the soccer Premier League.
HANOI - Vietnam says it hopes to license its first Internet service provider within weeks as part of a step-by-step opening to the World Wide Web.
FRANKFURT - Online-Dienst Germany.Net, the free-to-use Internet service, says it is receiving 500 new registrations daily and has a total of 200,000 clients.
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

PARIS - French anti-tobacco activists hail the landmark accord reached between U.S. authorities and cigarette companies, but the tobacco industry and financial analysts say such a settlement is unlikely in France.

JOHANNESBURG - African-American investors who backed Pepsi's abortive return to South Africa are looking for ways to revive the venture, Business Day newspaper reports. This comes after Pepsi pulled the plug on South African bottler New Age Beverages last month.

LONDON - British drinks firms face controversy over the launch of frozen alcoholic ices called "ice lollies". Up to three versions of ice lollies are to be sold in Britain's pubs, clubs and off-licences, and they will have the same alcohol content as strong lager, says the Express newspaper.

TOKYO - Nissan Motor Co Ltd says it plans drastically to reduce the types of Nissan car platforms by the year 2000 in order to cut production and development costs. Nissan currently has 15 platforms used in domestic and overseas production.
DUBAI - Saudi Arabia has warned traders they will be fined and their businesses closed if they sell counterfeit merchandise, part of the kingdom's crackdown on copyright violations.

BRUSSELS - Belgian retailer Delhaize signs long-term cooperation agreement with Indonesia's Salim Group to develop a supermarket chain in Indonesia. It expects to open 50 "Super Indo" stores in the next five years.

KUALA LUMPUR - U.S. based cosmetics company Avon, a pioneer in door-to-door direct sales techniques, says its biggest growth markets are in Asia. "Our growth in Asia-Pacific has been 35 percent a year for the past three years," against nine to ten percent annual growth in Europe and the U.S., says a company spokesman.

SEOUL - South Korea's Daewoo Group will soon be assembling cars in China, selling cars in the United States and sending hundreds of its top executives to markets worldwide. "Global expansion has emerged as an issue of survival for us," says group chairman Kim Woo-choong.
CONSUMER TRENDS:

LONDON - Communications overkill -- a product of the 1990s world of e-mail, voicemail, fax and the internet -- is starting to impair companies' efficiency and to drive workers crazy, according to a report by U.S. office products company Pitney Bowes.

LONDON - Insurers fear a growing "compensation culture" in which almost anyone feels they can sue for damages for almost anything. The landmark deal to settle tobacco litigation in the U.S. has emphasised the huge risks insurers could face from individual lawsuits, class actions and government-sponsored action related to a range of products from alcohol, to cars and drugs, according to insurance experts.

VALLETTA - Malta is planning to open two or three casinos in luxury hotels and to let in 18-year-olds in order to boost tourism. But in an effort to reduce the dangers of gambling for the Maltese, casino advertising in areas not frequented by tourists will be banned, says Malta's Tourism minister.
